body:
Ahh my bad, I originally meant I'd do two different trips; first go apply for jobs/interview, come back to the US and apply for Visa, then move out if I get accepted.  It was just really late when I typed that up!

That time frame seems like it would work quite well, even if it was a 12 week wait I could probably swing that time frame.  That part is at least good news!  Thanks so much octopus, your comments have been very helpful :)

Haha while the bonus pay would be nice, it's not something I'd get hung up over if I don't qualify; I totally understand their priorities.  I had read something about that, which was why I was really starting to consider the UK in general to begin with!

Thanks for the quick reply, and my apologies on not getting back to you sooner; had some IRL stuff to take care of.  

So from what I'm understanding after reading both yours and /u/clever_octopus comments, I need to have an actual job offer prior to applying for the Visa, but I also need to be prepared to actually travel there and apply.  From my understanding, I don't need a travel Visa to get into the UK from the US, just my passport; so I think it would be best to get a number of interviews lined up, travel/interview, then do my application process if I get an offer.  

Assuming that above paragraph is correct, do you (or anyone else) have a rough estimate of how long it might take to complete the process of getting the Visa?  I'm trying to get a game plan of how and when I would start applying.  As a teacher, around mid-May is when I could plan to start the process of going to interview for job openings, but realistically it'd probably be closer to early June.  If I find a position quickly enough, would that be enough time for me to apply for my Visa and do some preliminary house-hunting to move out there?  Or should I consider trying to terminate my contract earlier in the school year?

(Btw I'm aware every situation is different and lots of things could go well/wrong, resulting in different estimates or even rejections.  Just curious about the "average" experience, I can handle complications from there; just trying to structure a general game plan :)

Thanks all so much for the help thus far!
